name: llama.cpp
sycl_build: set-up (ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ builds via icpx -fsycl, AOT bmg-g31, links oneMKL; registers as backend SYCL0)

e2e_cases.name: qwen3-0.6b-debug
e2e_cases.cmd: build/bin/llama-cli -m /workspace/models/Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf --reasoning off --single-turn -p 'The capital of France is' -n 32 --temp 0 --seed 42 -ngl 99

e2e_cases.name: qwen3-8b-e2e
e2e_cases.cmd: build/bin/llama-cli -m /host/root/code/models/Qwen3-8B-GGUF/Qwen3-8B-Q8_0.gguf --reasoning off --single-turn -p 'The capital of France is' -n 32 --temp 0 --seed 42 -ngl 99

integration.entrypoint: build/bin/llama-cli (real user entrypoint); also build/bin/llama-perplexity for accuracy, build/bin/test-backend-ops for op-level correctness
integration.notes: kind=application (llama-cli e2e driver exists). CUDA backend (ggml/src/ggml-cuda) is the reference source; 68 .cu kernel files. SYCL header/cmake options already stubbed by upstream llama.cpp scaffolding but ggml-sycl/ implementation directory does not exist -- must be created from scratch, mirroring ggml-cuda structure per project convention (upstream llama.cpp has a real ggml-sycl backend we do not copy from -- hand-written per sycl-migration skill).

sycl_tla.notes: Set enabled=true and resolve include (from config targets.sycl_tla) when a kernel targets sycl-tla.

reference.source: CPU backend (ggml-cpu) via test-backend-ops for op-level unit tests; llama-cli -ngl 0 (CPU) greedy decode + llama-perplexity for e2e (per config.integration.workload_reference)
reference.notes: How golden reference outputs are obtained for accuracy checks (CUDA capture / CPU / analytical).
